thread.title: St. Pete's Jabil, maker of iPhone casings, overcame challenges to come out better than expected in 3Q

author: Margie Manning
title: St. Pete's Jabil, maker of iPhone casings, overcame challenges to come out better than expected in 3Q
text: – Finance Editor, Tampa Bay Business Journal Jun 15, 2018, 7:13am EDT Jabil Inc.’s efforts over the past several years to mix up its customer and products led to financial results that exceeded expectations in the third quarter of fiscal year 2018. The results represent a “diversified stream of earnings ... that’s sustainable as we head into fiscal year 2019” for Jabil (NYSE: JBL), an electronics manufacturing and services firm based in St. Petersburg, CEO Mark Mondello said during a conference call with analysts late Thursday. Jabil is a major employer and philanthropic contributor, so its strong financial results have an impact on the Tampa Bay area. The company decided earlier this year to build a new headquarters on its current campus in the Gateway area at Roosevelt Boulevard and Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Street N. Jabil reported revenue of $5.4 billion for the three months ended May 31, up 21 percent from the same quarter in 2017. Net income was $42.5 million, or 25 cents a share, compared to a loss of $25.2 million, or 14 cents a share, a year ago. The better-than-expected results for Q3 2018 occurred despite two distinct challenges, Mondello said. “First were unanticipated factory costs caused by broad-based material and component constraints, and second were lingering cost overruns within our packaging business. These two issues combined — one macro and one more micro in nature — cost us $12 million to $13 million during the quarter. The good news is both challenges are temporary and both will dissipate,” Mondello said. Mondello rarely mentions specific customers, but about 24 percent of Jabil’s sales last year came from Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL). Jabil makes casings for iPhones, and Barron’s speculated that the “challenging components market” likely was a reference to a slowdown in smartphone sales. Jabil is projecting revenue of $5.2 billion to $5.6 billion for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2018, which ends on Aug. 31. That would increase Jabil’s revenue for the full year to nearly $22 billion. The company expects earnings per share for the current quarter to be between 38 cents and 65 cents. The earnings report, released after the market closed on Thursday, pushed Jabil’s stock price up nearly 3 percent in after-hours trading, to $30.50 a share. The company also said it would buy back an additional $350 million in stock in fiscal 2019. It’s repurchased about $860 million in stock over the past two years.
